source_policy: Every substantive claim uses an object-local source identifier. Aliases retain title, author, publisher, year, locator, URL, source type, and original work ID; supports are scoped to G3 evidence IDs.

sources.notes: Primary biblical text. G3 local alias of CKL source 'genesis-1-50'; this record references the same work. The historical source record and its ownership are unchanged.
sources.title: Genesis 1-50

sources.author: Nahum M. Sarna
sources.notes: Jewish scholarly commentary. G3 local alias of CKL source 'sarna-genesis'; this record references the same publication/work. The historical source record and its ownership are unchanged.
sources.title: The JPS Torah Commentary: Genesis

sources.author: Victor P. Hamilton
sources.notes: NICOT commentary representing a conservative evangelical scholarly perspective. G3 local alias of CKL source 'hamilton-genesis-1-17'; this record references the same publication/work. The historical source record and its ownership are unchanged.
sources.title: The Book of Genesis, Chapters 1-17

sources.author: Bustenay Oded
sources.notes: Socio-cultural analysis of Genesis 10; used for the table’s social and political categories, not as proof that each eponym denotes only an individual.
sources.title: The Table of Nations (Genesis 10) — A Socio-cultural Approach

sources.author: Thomas Hieke
sources.locator: Berlin Studies of the Ancient World 29, pp. 23-40
sources.notes: Chapter argues that genealogy and kinship language organize a narrated spatial/ethnographic order; employed as one scholarly model, not a claim of literal biological descent for every name.
sources.title: Die Völkertafel von Genesis 10 als genealogische Raumordnung. Form, Funktion, Geographie

sources.author: Mary Katherine Y. H. Hom
sources.notes: Examines the wording and moral evaluation of Nimrod; supports preserving interpretive alternatives around “before YHWH” and hunting.
sources.title: “A Mighty Hunter before YHWH”: Genesis 10:9 and Moral-Theological Evaluation of Nimrod

sources.author: Yigal Levin
sources.notes: Historical identification is a scholarly reconstruction and is recorded only as a proposal, not an established identification.
sources.title: Nimrod the Mighty, King of Kish, King of Sumer and Akkad

sources.author: David M. Carr
sources.locator: Chapters 4 and 7, especially Genesis 11:10-26 and Genesis 9:18-11:9
sources.notes: A source-critical account of Genesis 1-11; models of composition are presented as scholarly proposals in a contested field.
sources.title: The Formation of Genesis 1-11: Biblical and Other Precursors

sources.author: Jonathan Grossman
sources.notes: Studies the literary etymology in Genesis 11 and its relation to Babylon’s name; does not collapse Hebrew wordplay into historical Akkadian etymology.
sources.title: The Double Etymology of Babel in Genesis 11

sources.author: Chris Gousmett
sources.notes: Surveys interpretation of Genesis 11:1-9 and the relation of the Babel episode to the Table of Nations; its interpretive account is not a scientific linguistic history.
sources.title: The confusion of language in the interpretation of Genesis 11

sources.author: Kacie Klamm
sources.notes: Study of the language and Babylonian background of Genesis 11:1-9; used for bounded cultural/literary comparison.
sources.title: On the Meaning of Language in Genesis 11:1-9 and Its Babylonian Background

sources.author: Andrew R. George
sources.notes: Peer-reviewed study of Babylonian ziggurat history and cuneiform evidence. It supports comparison to Babylonian monumental architecture, not identification of an excavated structure as the Genesis tower.
sources.title: The Tower of Babel: Archaeology, history and cuneiform texts

sources.author: Institut national de recherches archéologiques préventives / French Ministry of Culture
sources.locator: Architecture of the ziggurat; construction and reconstruction history of Babylonian Etemenanki
sources.notes: Institutional archaeology overview. Its Etemenanki reconstruction and construction phases describe one Babylonian comparator, not the identity or date of the Genesis tower.
sources.title: Architecture of the ziggurat

sources.author: Musée du Louvre
sources.locator: Collection record SB 1700; inscription concerning Babylon and Etemenanki
sources.notes: Museum record for a primary royal inscriptional object. Supports the existence of royal building claims concerning Babylon’s ziggurat; it does not attest the Genesis narrative.
sources.title: Royal votive cylinder of Nebuchadnezzar II (Louvre SB 1700)

sources.author: Jean Connan and Olivier Deschesne
sources.notes: Archaeological/material study of bitumen sources and uses in the ancient Near East, including construction applications.
sources.title: Archaeological Bitumen: Identification, Origins and Uses of an Ancient Near Eastern Material

sources.author: Sargon II; edited by Grant Frame
sources.locator: RINAP 2, Q006534; Dur-Šarrukīn building and naming statements
sources.notes: Primary royal inscription used only as comparative evidence for a king’s naming and building claims; no identification with Nimrod is implied.
sources.publisher: Royal Inscriptions of the Neo-Assyrian Period, RINAP 2 / ORACC
sources.title: The Annals of Sargon II, Q006534

sources.author: Ronald S. Hendel
sources.locator: Textual notes on Genesis 11:10-26 and related primeval-history witnesses
sources.notes: Critical study of Genesis textual witnesses. Textual chronology differences are reported without assuming one textual tradition resolves the question.
sources.title: The Text of Genesis 1-11: Textual Studies and Critical Edition

sources.author: H. W. F. Saggs
sources.notes: Reviews the identification problem; southern Ur is strongly favored in modern scholarship, while alternative proposals have a history and should not be misstated as impossible.
sources.title: Ur of the Chaldees: A Problem of Identification

sources.author: David M. Goldenberg
sources.locator: Study of the history of interpretation of Genesis 9:20-27
sources.notes: Reception history documents later racialized readings; it is not evidence that Genesis 9 or 10 encodes modern race theory.
sources.title: The Curse of Ham: Race and Slavery in Early Judaism, Christianity, and Islam

sources.author: Robert R. Wilson
sources.locator: Comparative study of biblical genealogy and social history
sources.notes: Classic study treating genealogy as a social and historiographic form; not a one-to-one biological model for every genealogy.
sources.title: Genealogy and History in the Biblical World
